title.value: Resting state EEG power spectrum and functional connectivity in autism: a cross-sectional analysis
title.justification: The value is the exact title provided at the beginning of the research paper. It accurately captures the focus of the study, which involves EEG power spectrum and functional connectivity analysis in the context of autism.
title.quote: Resting state EEG power spectrum and functional connectivity in autism: a cross‐sectional analysis

extractions.description: The paper investigates resting state EEG parameters in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) compared to neurotypical (NT) controls. It analyzes EEG power spectrum and functional connectivity to identify potential differences in brain activity between these groups. The study specifically examines the variability, mean differences, and multivariate patterns across a cohort with IQ > 75 from childhood to adulthood, employing machine learning techniques for classification.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on autism spectrum disorder and neuronal features as opposed to environmental or sustainability-related themes. While the research is scientifically relevant, it does not address climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Understanding the development of the neuronal circuitry underlying autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is critical to shed light into its etiology and for the development of treatment options.

primary_category.justification: The research does not engage with sustainable development, climate change, or ecological themes. It is focused on autism and neuroscience, which do not align with the categories of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: ASD is heterogeneous with diverse clinical presentations and frequent comorbidities including epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety and depression.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes are identifiable as the paper is solely focused on the biomedical analysis of autism and EEG data which is outside the scope of sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We investigated differences in resting state EEG parameters between autistic and neurotypical individuals with average to high intellectual abilities from childhood to adulthood in a large and well-controlled cohort.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no sub-category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development applicable to the paper, as its core focus is on the inherent variability and features of autism spectrum disorder within a neuroscience framework.
primary_sub_category.quote: We quantified resting state EEG alpha peak metrics, power spectrum (PS, 2–32 Hz) and functional connectivity (FC) in 411 children, adolescents and adults.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper strictly deals with autism-related neuroscience and does not extend to any relevant sustainable development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We focused on diagnostic effects and compared ASD and NT groups.

applications.justification: The paper does not cover applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. It addresses the neurological aspects of autism.
applications.quote: To assess whether a multivariate combination of EEG features could better separate ASD and NT participants.

new_primary_category.justification: The study is clearly aligned with research into neurodevelopmental disorders, particularly focusing on EEG-based markers in autism. This fits outside the current predefined categories of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Resting state EEG provides a window into spontaneous local and long-range neuronal synchronization and has been investigated in many ASD studies.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically analyzes EEG data in relation to autism spectrum disorder, forming a detailed scientific analysis focused on this condition, which warrants a new sub-category under neurodevelopmental disorders research.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We performed analyses in source-space using individual head models derived from the participants’ MRIs.
